text:
alex: seeing a weird tail-latency bump on the llama-3-13b canary after the kernel selector change. median fine, p95 up ~120ms for short chats (~40 tokens).

mira: ugh. any obvious tracer output? selector should prefer int8 matmul path for that headdim.

alex: attaching quick profile snippet from the canary run:
```
[profiling] kernel=matmul_fp16_generic time=0.98ms
[profiling] kernel=matmul_int8_opt time=2.11ms
[profiling] kv_cache: hits=0.86 miss=0.14
[serving] batch_size=4 seq=40 head_dim=128 hidden=5120 rope_theta=1.0
```

cheng: wait head_dim 128 + hidden 5120 -> 40 heads? that math looks off for our llama-3 build. expected heads=32. if head count mismatch, kernel selector can pick suboptimal tiling.

samir: +1. We had a change that computed heads = hidden / head_dim but forgot to floor/align to 32 multiple. selector fallback to generic kernel then.

mira: so it's a head/alignment issue. But why kv_cache hit lower? should be independent.

alex: hypothesis: rope_theta defaulting to 1.0 for this production checkpoint causes slightly different rotary phase wrap leading to cache key variance for early tokens, causing extra KV stores on prefix reuse. small but visible for interactive flows.

julia: interesting. Have we seen rope_theta drift between Llama 2/3 checkpoints? some exporters bake a scaled theta.

cheng: yes — older conversion script applied rope scaling of 0.97 for 13B. Newer loaders set 1.0. Mixing checkpoints + runtime defaults can break cache reuse heuristics if we use exact-match cache keys.

samir: two actionable items: 1) make kernel selector align heads to supported tiling (round to nearest supported head multiple) and add a strict-override flag for experiments; 2) normalize rope_theta during load to a canonical value or add a cache-key-insensitive fingerprint.

alex: i ran a quick repro with a manual override: kernel.force=matmul_int8_opt; rope_theta=0.97; result: p95 back down ~70ms.

mira: can you paste the override config?

alex:
```json
{
  "model": "llama-3-13b",
  "runtime_overrides": {
    "kernel.force": "matmul_int8_opt",
    "rope_theta": 0.97,
    "heads_align": 32
  },
  "batching": { "max_batch": 8, "latency_slo_ms": 120 }
}
```

cheng: nice. Also add a selector log if selected kernel != expected for (heads, head_dim) combos so we can alert earlier.

samir: added alert rule idea: selector-mismatch-rate > 1% for 5m -> page eng-runtime.

julia: longer-term we should: a) add per-model rope_theta metadata in model catalog, b) make KV cache key generation resilient to tiny numeric differences (quantize float phases to canonical bucket).

ops-bot: deploy-canary: llm-runtime v4.12 deployed to canary pool at 2105003000 by samir :rocket:

mira: for immediate mitigation, can we roll a config patch to force-head-align and rope normalization for the canary pool? low-risk.

alex: yes tested locally, will build a runtime-config patch and bump canary (no model reload).

samir: FYI I profiled a few other shapes — llama-2-13b with head_dim=128 + hidden 5120 didn't show regression because its rope_theta baked to 0.97 already. supports the mismatch hypothesis.

cheng: i'll open a tiny PR to selector to add alignment + verbose logging. alex, can you attach perf diff after canary patch?

alex: will post diffs in this thread after canary runs complete. initial ETA ~30-45m.

julia: also log suggestion: add a small unit test: export a model with rope_theta=0.97 then load with default 1.0 and assert kv_cache key stability for a short prefix sequence.

alex: good call. adding that to testplan.

samir: thanks all. low-risk rollout if canary looks good.

alex: update: canary rolled, p95 improved to baseline. attaching short diff numbers:
```
before: p95=410ms p99=780ms
after:  p95=290ms p99=540ms
alloc: improved tail by ~30% on small-batch interactive.
```

mira: yay. leave the selector alert active for 24h.

cheng: PR link: https://git.internal/redwood/selector/pulls/1234 (adds alignment + logs).

alex: closing loop — follow-ups: model-catalog rope metadata, unit test, selector alert. i'll create tickets. :white_check_mark:
